name: Keep your Marines informed
definition: Marines are inquisitive by nature. To promote efficiency and morale, you should inform your Marines of all happenings and give reasons why things are to be done.

rows.situation: When you hand someone a task
rows.under: Gives the task and none of the reason. They cannot adapt when the path breaks.
rows.justRight: Says what to do and why, so they can carry on when you are not there.
rows.over: Gives a speech about context and they still cannot name the next step.

rows.situation: When a decision will change their week
rows.under: Lets them find out when the work lands differently.
rows.justRight: Tells them as soon as you can, including what stays the same.
rows.over: Forwards every rumor so they spend the week decoding noise.

rows.situation: When they need to act without you
rows.under: Holds the picture in your head and answers one question at a time.
rows.justRight: Gives them enough of the situation to do the job intelligently and to use their own judgment.
rows.over: Dumps the whole file and calls that informing them.

rows.situation: When time or privacy limits what you can say
rows.under: Goes silent and lets them invent the story.
rows.justRight: Says what you can, says what you cannot, and tells them when more will come.
rows.over: Hints until they guess, and the guess is worse than the truth.

rows.situation: When you will be gone and the work will not
rows.under: Leaves them a task list with no picture of the situation.
rows.justRight: Leaves the goal, the constraints, and who to ask, so they can continue without you.
rows.over: Writes a manual so long that nobody can find the one decision they will have to make.
